decision: wrote CONTRACT.md defining complete (C1-C7) and verified (V1-V7) before modeling
why: user asked for explicit done/verification definitions first; user is afk so the contract must be self-enforcing

decision: pinned the zeldaret/oot decomp as the only source of truth
why: the decomp is the game's actual rules; wikis disagree and can't be rerun

decision: scope chosen mechanically: ENEMY or BOSS category, or a DamageTable, or an AT_TYPE_ENEMY collider
why: taste-picked enemy lists miss things (Leever is ACTORCAT_MISC, traps hurt Link); a rule the extractor applies can't drift
result: 111 actors, 48 damage tables, 323 elements, 946 action funcs

decision: real time abstracted to beats, space to range bands, AI to phases, one actor per encounter
why: MAPS 2 has no time, positions, or composition; abstracting the same way everywhere keeps encounters comparable

decision: one typed ActorSpec per actor plus a LinkSpec; a generator turns them into beat-structured encounter nets
why: same rules everywhere and the numbers come straight from the decomp inventory, so nobody hand-copies 32-entry tables
result: Keese encounter generated, round-trips, 0 checker errors

decision: delegated Link's spec to an opus researcher; 24 of 32 damage types emitted, 8 excluded with grep evidence
why: player code is 16k lines; isolate it from the coordinator context
result: 172 cites walked, 2 fixed by the researcher

decision: indexed verbs by one required input state in engine.whoseTurn
why: Keese with full kit took 197s for 251k positions; most time was scanning every verb at every marking

decision: replaced one full-kit loadout per age with five small shared kits
why: full kit explodes magic x health x timers; the encounter's analysis is the sum of its kits, not the product
result: Keese real-Link run killed after 10 min before the change

decision: hit resolution collapsed to one swing state per damage type, a default verb per type, and per-phase verbs only where a phase differs
why: Keese had 3661 verbs (attacks x 33 phases x lens copies)

decision: fractional per-beat costs (burn 1/8 frames, lens 1/80 frames) become a whole amount every q beats with a counter
why: rounding lens to 1 per beat would drain magic 4x too fast
result: burn 5 per 2 beats, lens 1 per 4 beats

decision: verified a shield block still counts as an AT hit, so a Keese flies off after a block
why: Keese steps send it to Stay on AT_HIT; needed to know if blocks do the same
result: blocked and landed bites share the step
